title: Usability study plan — Optimization Suggestions view (beta) | Comprehension of savings + risk
linked_artifacts: Slack: #design thread 1771703310 (risk badge copy and contrast)
content:
Last updated: 2026-02-24 (GM)

Context
We’re shipping a beta “Optimization suggestions” experience in Redwood Console (Redwood Optimize) focused on batching and caching recommendations. The Suggestions view surfaces:
1) Estimated savings ($/day and %)
2) Estimated performance impact (p50/p95 latency deltas)
3) Risk level (Low/Medium/High) + explanation and guardrails

This study evaluates whether target users understand the savings and risk information well enough to make safe decisions and trust the system (without interpreting estimates as guarantees).

Primary research goals
1) Comprehension: Do users correctly interpret “Estimated savings” (not guaranteed) and understand what inputs/assumptions drive the estimate?
2) Risk understanding: Do users understand what the risk label means (performance/reliability risk), what it does NOT mean (security risk), and how to mitigate it?
3) Decision-making: Can users identify which suggestions are worth exploring/applying given their own goals (cost vs latency) and constraints?
4) Information hierarchy: Do users find the right details (why we recommend, assumptions, staleness, confidence band) without getting overwhelmed?
5) Actionability: Do users understand the “how to enable” / next step path (deep links to config) and rollouts safety cues?

Study type
Moderated remote usability sessions using an interactive prototype (and/or staging build behind feature flag if stable). 45–60 minutes each.

Key hypotheses
H1: Users will confuse “risk” with security/compliance risk unless we explicitly label it as “Latency/Reliability risk” (or clarify in tooltip).
H2: Users will over-trust the savings number unless the UI consistently shows assumptions + confidence and uses conservative language (e.g., “estimate”, “expected range”).
H3: Users will use the list view to triage by savings and risk; they will open the details drawer primarily when risk is Medium/High, or when savings is very large.
H4: Users will struggle to interpret p50 vs p95 latency deltas unless we frame it in user-visible impact (tail latency / SLO risk) and show baseline.
H5: Staleness (“computed as of …”) will be overlooked unless placed near the headline estimate.

Participant recruitment
Target profile (beta personas)
- Role: ML engineers, platform engineers, infra engineers, senior backend engineers who own production latency/cost tradeoffs.
- Experience: Has shipped/operates an LLM feature in production OR actively preparing for production.
- Familiarity: Understands basic concepts of batching/caching at a high level (does not need to be a CUDA expert).
- Responsibilities: Owns or heavily influences production settings, SLOs, and/or cost management.

Screening criteria (must-have)
- Has monitored latency (p50/p95) and cost for an API/service before.
- Can describe a recent tradeoff they made between performance and cost.
- Comfortable reading dashboards/tables and acting on recommendations.

Nice-to-have (quota targets)
- 30–40% users in regulated orgs (care about private/VPC/on-prem considerations even though this beta is Console UX).
- Mix of high QPS and moderate QPS workloads.
- Mix of “cost-first” and “latency-first” priorities.

Exclusion criteria
- Participants who have not worked with production services or do not engage with performance/cost metrics.
- Participants who only want a “one-button optimize everything” experience (beta non-goal; may skew feedback).

Sample size and quotas
- N=8 sessions total
  - 4 internal (dogfood): Redwood engineers/PMs not directly building the feature (avoid project team members)
  - 4 external (design partners / beta accounts)
- If we see high variance or unclear findings: add +4 external follow-ups focused only on risk comprehension.

Recruitment sources
- Internal: ask Engineering/Product leads to nominate participants from adjacent teams.
- External: coordinate with CS (Miguel Santos) + PM (Marissa Cole / Aditya Rao) to recruit from beta target accounts with adequate telemetry maturity.

Incentives
- External: $150–$200 USD gift card (or equivalent) for 60 minutes.
- Internal: no incentive.

Materials / stimulus
- Prototype of Suggestions list + details drawer including:
  - Savings ($/day, %) and an “Assumptions” section
  - p50/p95 latency deltas + baseline latency (or clear framing if baseline not in prototype)
  - Risk badge + tooltip + “Why this is risky” explanation
  - “Computed as of …” staleness indicator
  - Deep link CTA(s) to configuration pages (batching/caching)
  - Empty state variants (insufficient telemetry; feature not enabled)

- Alternate copy variants (A/B within session):
  - Variant A: “Risk: Medium” with tooltip clarifying “Latency & reliability risk”
  - Variant B: “Latency risk: Medium” (explicit)
  - Variant C: “Operational risk: Medium” (we suspect this performs worse; included to validate)

- (Optional) 1-page primer shown only if participant is stuck: definitions of batching, prefix caching / KV cache.

Session logistics
- Platform: Zoom + screen share, recorded with consent.
- Session length: 60 minutes (target 50 min + buffer).
- Moderator: George Mbatha
- Note taker: Kenji Nakamura or Alicia Perez (rotate)
- Observers: Max 3 silent observers; PM/Eng can attend but must remain muted.

Consent + privacy
- We will not collect API keys, proprietary prompts, or customer data.
- If external participants refer to sensitive details, moderator will redirect.
- Recordings stored in restricted Drive folder; summarized findings shared broadly.

Success metrics (usability + comprehension)
Quantitative (per task)
- Task success rate (Complete / Partial / Fail)
- Time on task
- Confidence rating (1–5): “How confident are you in what this means / what you’d do next?”
- Comprehension check accuracy (scored):
  - Savings interpretation: understands it’s estimated and conditional
  - Risk interpretation: correctly explains what “risk” refers to and identifies mitigation steps
  - Latency deltas: correctly interprets p95 change and its implication

Qualitative
- Top confusion points (language, layout, missing context)
- Trust indicators (what increases/decreases trust)
- Decision rationale: what they would apply vs defer and why

Target thresholds for beta readiness (proposed)
- ≥ 80% of participants accurately explain “risk” in our intended framing without moderator correction
- ≥ 80% avoid interpreting savings as guaranteed after reading the UI once
- ≥ 70% can identify at least one safe next step (e.g., “start with Low risk,” “canary,” “apply to one route”) using the UI’s cues

Core tasks
Task 0: Warm-up (5 min)
- Tell me about your role and how you think about inference cost and latency today.
- What tools/dashboards do you use? What’s the hardest part?

Task 1: First impressions (List view) (8 min)
Prompt: “You’ve opened the Optimization Suggestions page. Talk out loud: what is this page showing you?”
Success: Participant identifies suggestions are recommendations for cost optimization; notices savings + risk; does not assume auto-apply.
Follow-ups:
- What would you click first and why?
- What do you expect will happen if you click into a row?

Task 2: Interpret a Low-risk caching suggestion (Details drawer) (10 min)
Scenario: Route /chat/completions, model X. Suggestion: enable prefix caching; savings: ~$120/day (8–12% range shown); p95 latency: -10ms to +5ms; Risk: Low.
Questions:
- In your own words, what is this recommending?
- What does “$120/day estimated” mean to you? What would you expect to happen in billing?
- What would you check before enabling?
- How would you roll this out safely?
Comprehension checks:
- Ask participant to point to where the estimate comes from / assumptions.
- Ask what “computed as of” means and whether they would trust it if it’s 7 days old.

Task 3: Interpret a Medium/High-risk batching suggestion (10–12 min)
Scenario: Route /summarize, strict latency SLO. Suggestion: increase max batch size; savings: ~$400/day; p95 latency: +60ms; Risk: High.
Questions:
- Why is this flagged as High risk (based on what you see)?
- Would you apply it? Under what conditions?
- What guardrails would you want?
- If you had to take action, what would you do next in the product?
Comprehension checks:
- What do p50 and p95 mean here?
- Does “risk” mean security/compliance risk to you? If not, what does it mean?

Task 4: Compare and triage (sorting/filtering) (8 min)
Prompt: “You have 10 minutes before a cost review. Find the top 2 opportunities you’d bring to your team, with minimal risk.”
Expected behaviors:
- Uses filters (risk level, model, route, region) and sorting (savings, risk, confidence)
- Opens details for final selection
Measures:
- Whether they can accomplish the triage without getting lost
- What criteria they use

Task 5: “Apply” path comprehension (6–8 min)
Prompt: “You decided to try one suggestion. Show me what you’d do next.”
We’re testing:
- Whether the deep link CTA is clear
- Whether users expect immediate change vs a rollout flow
- Whether they understand this beta does not auto-apply
Probe:
- “What would you want to happen next ideally?” vs “What do you think happens today?”

Task 6: Empty/insufficient telemetry state (optional, 5 min)
Show the empty state: “Insufficient telemetry to generate suggestions.”
Questions:
- What do you think is missing?
- What would you do next?
- Is the CTA clear (enable telemetry / wait for backfill)?

Moderator script (high-level)
Intro (2 min)
- Thanks, context: evaluating a beta Console feature.
- No right/wrong answers; we’re testing the design.
- Please think out loud.
- Ask permission to record.

During tasks
- Use neutral prompts: “What are you thinking?” “What would you do next?”
- Avoid explaining concepts unless participant is blocked for >60 seconds.
- When probing comprehension, ask participants to reference the UI.

Wrap-up (5 min)
- What felt unclear or untrustworthy?
- What’s missing for you to act confidently?
- If you could change one thing on this page, what would it be?
- How likely would you be to use this weekly? (1–5) Why?

Data capture template (for note taker)
- Participant code / role / company type (startup/mid/enterprise)
- Task-by-task notes:
  - Success (C/P/F)
  - Time
  - Quotes
  - Confusions
  - Trust signals
  - Suggested improvements
- Comprehension score:
  - Savings (0/1)
  - Risk meaning (0/1)
  - p95 meaning (0/1)
  - Next step / rollout safety (0/1)

Analysis plan
- Immediately after each session: 10-minute debrief with observers; tag top 3 issues.
- After N=4: interim readout to Design/PM; decide whether to adjust copy before remaining sessions.
- Final synthesis:
  - Thematic clustering (risk comprehension, estimate trust, latency comprehension, actionability)
  - Severity rating (Critical: blocks correct decision; Major: slows; Minor: annoyance)
  - Recommendations with proposed copy/layout changes

Open questions to validate in study
1) Should we label it “Risk” vs “Latency/Reliability risk” vs “Operational risk”?
2) Do users understand confidence bands, or should we simplify to “confidence: high/medium/low”?
3) Are p50/p95 deltas enough, or do we need to show baseline and SLO threshold in the drawer?
4) Do users want a default filter to show only Low/Medium risk during beta?
5) Where should we place staleness so users notice it?

Operational notes / dependencies
- Need stable prototype with list view, drawer, filters, and at least 3 example suggestion rows.
- Need agreed copy for disclaimers: “Estimates are based on recent telemetry and may differ from actual results.”
- Ensure risk tooltip clarifies: “This reflects performance/reliability risk (latency/SLO impact), not security risk.”

Risks + mitigations
- Risk: Participants interpret estimates as a promise.
  - Mitigation: include explicit disclaimer and ask comprehension checks early.
- Risk: Participants lack context for batching/caching.
  - Mitigation: recruit for baseline familiarity; provide optional 1-page primer only if stuck.
- Risk: Prototype doesn’t match real config flows.
  - Mitigation: frame tasks as ‘what would you expect’; validate deep-link clarity rather than full apply flow.

Proposed timeline
- 2026-02-10 to 2026-02-14: finalize prototype + script; recruit participants
- 2026-02-17 to 2026-02-21: run sessions (4 internal + 2 external)
- 2026-02-24 to 2026-02-28: run remaining external sessions; synthesis + readout

Requested decisions (from PM/Design)
- Which 2–3 copy variants should we test for the risk label?
- Confirm whether we’ll show confidence bands or just a confidence label in beta.

Owner
George Mbatha (UX Research)
